commits.message:
[BugFix][KV Pool] Don't pin mamba speculative scratch blocks on save (#16329)

### What this PR does / why we need it

vLLM PR [#51358](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51358) made
the KV cache manager relocate Mamba speculative scratch blocks at chunk
boundaries. Relocation is intentionally fail-closed: the scratch block
must be exclusively owned (`ref_cnt == 1`) and unhashed before it can be
moved.

For hybrid Mamba workloads using speculative decoding and non-layerwise
AscendStore saves, `touch_sending_mamba_blocks()` previously pinned
every non-null Mamba block until the asynchronous save completed. That
included the speculative scratch tail, raising its reference count from
1 to 2. The next chunk-boundary relocation then failed the
writable-block assertion and terminated EngineCore.

This PR establishes each cache group's actual
`MambaSpec.num_speculative_blocks` as the single source of truth:

- Keeps `_infer_mamba_groups()` as the cache-spec normalization
boundary. It unwraps `UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs`, validates the supported
`mamba_cache_mode='align'`, and now returns `{group_id:
num_speculative_blocks}` instead of only group IDs.
- Passes the same per-group mapping to `RequestTracker`, so its Mamba
block-table mirror uses the same scratch-block count as the allocator.
- Excludes only each Mamba group's actual speculative scratch tail from
the asynchronous AscendStore pin set. Persisted state blocks remain
pinned until the worker acknowledgement.

Using the per-group value is important because the global speculative
token count is not always the number of Mamba scratch blocks. For
example, RecoverSSM can use speculative decoding while setting
`MambaSpec.num_speculative_blocks` to zero. Reading the global value
would incorrectly exclude real state blocks from asynchronous-send
protection.

`UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` is safe to represent with its first inner spec
here because vLLM only creates a uniform Mamba wrapper when every inner
spec is a `MambaSpec` with the same `num_speculative_blocks` and
compatible layout properties.

### Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?

No API or configuration changes.

Hybrid Mamba + speculative decoding workloads using AscendStore no
longer pin relocatable scratch blocks during asynchronous saves. The
intended persisted-state set is preserved, while zero-scratch groups now
keep all real state blocks protected correctly.

commits.message:
[BugFix][Model] Fix dense-MLP token mixing under sequence-parallel MoE for GLM-5.3-Flash (#16804)

### What this PR does / why we need it?
Fixes silent accuracy corruption (repetition, degraded outputs,
flattened logprobs) when serving GLM-5.3-Flash with sequence-parallel
MoE enabled (`--additional-config '{"enable_flashcomm1": true}'`, i.e.
`use_sequence_parallel_moe`).

`Glm5NextDecoderLayer` constructs the dense `Glm5NextMLP` layers without
propagating `use_sequence_parallel_moe` (GLM-5.3-Flash has 3 dense
layers: `mlp_layer_types = [dense, dense, dense, sparse, ...]`). Under
SP the decoder layer runs on TP-sharded activations (each TP rank holds
a different slice of
tokens), but the dense MLP kept standard weight TP:

- `gate_up_proj` computes partial intermediate channels for each rank's
own tokens,
- `down_proj` (`reduce_results=True`) then allreduces across the TP
group, **summing partial outputs of different tokens**,
- every rank ends up with identical garbage rows (a cross-token
mixture), which corrupts the residual stream from layer 0 onward and is
amplified by the subsequent MoE layers.

The fix passes `is_sequence_parallel=self.is_sequence_parallel` and
`reduce_results=not self.is_sequence_parallel`, so dense MLPs use
replicated weights with no collectives under SP — the exact pattern
already used for `Glm5NextMoE.shared_experts` in this file and for dense
`DeepseekV2MLP` layers upstream
(`vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_v2.py`).

Evidence (Ascend A3, tp4 x dp2, EP, W8A8, eager, 16-token TP-aligned
prompt, layer-wise tensor dumps comparing SP-on vs SP-off):

| checkpoint | SP-on vs SP-off |
| --- | --- |
| embed / layer-0 mHC-pre / attn_in | bitwise identical |
| `sp_reduce_scatter` internal check (`cat(shards)` vs `sum(partials)`)
| rel ~5e-3 (bf16 noise) |
| layer-0 attention (sum of TP partials vs baseline) | rel ~4.5e-3 |
| **layer-0/1/2 dense `mlp_out` (before fix)** | **73-104% relative
error, bitwise identical across all 4 TP ranks (allreduce signature)** |
| layer-0/1/2 dense `mlp_out` (after fix) | rel ~1e-3 (bf16 noise) |
| greedy output text + top logprobs (after fix) | match SP-off baseline
|
### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?
Yes — fixes incorrect outputs for GLM-5.3-Flash served with SP MoE
(`enable_flashcomm1` with dp>1, tp>1, EP). No configuration changes; the
memory cost of replicating 3 dense layers' weights per rank is
negligible.
### How was this patch tested?
Manual NPU validation on Ascend 910 A3 (8 cards, tp4 x dp2, EP, W8A8
quant, eager), vllm @ 84030bbe3, vllm-ascend main @ 9750add07 (fix
applies cleanly
on current main):

- SP-on vs SP-off greedy completions with `logprobs=5`: outputs diverge
before the fix, identical after.
- Layer-wise tensor comparison (embedding, mHC-pre, attention in/out,
MLP out, final pre-norm hidden states) on prefill and decode steps.
- Tested on AIME2026 with `93.33/100` accuracy.

AI assistance (opencode) was used for root-cause analysis (instrumented
layer-wise comparison harness); the change itself is 2 lines and was
reviewed and validated end-to-end by the submitter.

commits.message:
[Feature][KVCache] Support layerwise KV pool for Kimi-K3 hybrid KDA+MLA on the V2 model runner (#16320)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Extends the layerwise KV pool (`AscendStoreConnector` + `use_layerwise`,
enabled for Qwen3.5 GDN hybrids in #15479) to **Kimi-K3 hybrid KDA + MLA
models on the V2 model runner** (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`).

Kimi-K3's KDA (delta attention) layers reuse the GDN state layout but
bypass the standard attention layer, so they never went through the
`@maybe_transfer_kv_layer` decorator. Without per-layer hooks the pool
worker's `current_layer` counter desyncs (only the MLA layer advances
it) and the first multi-block prefill trips `thread: 0 save failed` in
`KVCacheStoreLayerSendingThread`.

This PR adds the same hooks that `ops/gdn.py` already has to the KDA
eager-break `_forward` body (`ops/kimi_kda.py`, +17 lines):
- `wait_for_kv_layer_from_connector` + `record_attention_compute_start`
right after the `attn_metadata` None check, before the conv/recurrent
kernels touch mamba state (this also orders the deferred per-layer mamba
state copy and the layer load)
- `maybe_save_kv_layer_to_connector` on the idle early-exit path and on
the normal exit path

**Scope note**: the mamba-hybrid per-layer copy deferral, the connector
V1/V2 duck-typing and the accompanying UTs required by this scenario
were **merged upstream in #15479** and are not duplicated here. An
`mla_v1.get_kv_cache_shape` `cache_dtype_str` signature fix that was
briefly carried in this PR was solved upstream by #15514 and has been
dropped.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API/config change. The layerwise KV pool now works for Kimi-K3
(KDA+MLA hybrid) under the V2 model runner; previously it crashed on the
first multi-block prefill.

### How was this patch tested?

Verified on Atlas 800I A3 (8 NPU) with the Kimi-K3-w4a8-4layer
checkpoint (reduced 4-layer debug build of the ModelSlim W4A8 quantized
model), TP=8, EP, eager, memcache backend (`device_sdma`),
`use_layerwise=true`, `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`:
- Service starts; `/health` 200; text requests 200
- Long-prefix repeats hit the external pool: 768-token block restored
per repeat request (`kvpool hit tokens: 768`); repeat latency 3.4s ->
0.57s
- Stress: 104/104 requests OK (8-way concurrency, 90% repeat rate),
external prefix cache hit rate 64.6%, zero worker errors
- AIS-Bench A/B vs vLLM HBM prefix caching (prefix dataset: input 16088
/ output 50, 400 requests, concurrency 8, repeat_rate 0.9): **TTFT avg
1515ms -> 608ms (-60%), TTFT P90 5966ms -> 312ms (-95%), input
throughput 42.2k -> 65.1k tok/s (+54%)** at equal token-level hit rate
(85.93% both). The gain comes from restoring KDA states on hits, which
HBM prefix caching cannot cover (it only caches the MLA layer KV, the
KDA layers still recompute).

Remaining: MTP path needs validation once a Kimi-K3 checkpoint with
`num_nextn_predict_layers > 0` MTP weights is available (the 4-layer
debug checkpoint ships none).

commits.message:
[Feature][KV Pool] Support and optimize Mooncake hybrid layerwise transfer (#16747)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR adds Mooncake layerwise KV pool support for hybrid-attention
cache layouts and optimizes the layerwise data path for long
shared-prefix workloads such as DeepSeek-V4 Flash.

- Build group-aware Mooncake range sessions for multiple KV cache
groups, including different block sizes and sparse reachability masks.
- Derive object identity from the canonical layout digest, group ID, and
per-group block size without duplicating cache-family labels in the key.
- Normalize scheduler/worker layout fingerprints across
`UniformTypeKVCacheSpecs` packaging while retaining dtype and
cache-geometry isolation.
- Skip objects that are already readable in the pool before opening PUT
sessions, reducing redundant writes for repeated prefixes and concurrent
DP ranks.
- Keep future-layer GET prefetch asynchronous and use a backend-internal
PUT backlog of eight tasks instead of draining both queues after every
attention layer.
- Preserve transfer safety by draining both queues during full teardown
and waiting for the final layer SAVE before source buffers can be
reused.
- Preserve supported retention arguments across cache-manager signatures
and add a no-split range-metadata fast path.
- Document the hybrid layout, internal timing policy, limitations, and
validation workflow.

The asynchronous policy is backend-internal and exposes no runtime
tuning variables. It keeps future-layer GET prefetch running and allows
up to eight unfinished SEND tasks; errors and teardown still drain both
queues completely.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Mooncake layerwise KV pool transfer can be used with
hybrid-attention cache groups. The transfer scheduling policy is
internal and introduces no new environment variables.

### How was this patch tested?

- Rebased onto current `vllm-ascend/main` (`7a0aaebca`).
- `ruff check` passed for all changed Python files and related unit
tests.
- `python -m compileall` passed for the changed Python modules.
- `test_kv_transfer.py`: 33 passed, 26 subtests passed in the local mock
environment.
- Targeted layout/retention regression tests: 4 passed.
- Isolated lifecycle probes verified final-layer SAVE waiting and full
receive-queue draining.
- Markdown lint passed for the feature guide.

Real NPU and distributed Mooncake performance validation is still
required and is not claimed by this PR.

[Feature] Enable GLM-5.3-Flash PD disaggregation on Model Runner V2 (#16755)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enables GLM-Next (GLM-5.3-Flash) prefill/decode disaggregation on Model
Runner V2 with `MooncakeConnectorV2`, for both equal TP (P=TP4 / D=TP4)
and unequal TP (P=TP8 / D=DP2xTP4).

GLM-Next could not run PD on MRV2 because of three structural gaps:

1. **Granularity mismatch.** MRV2 hands metadata builders
kernel-granularity specs (`block_size` == the C128 SFA kernel size),
while the scheduler, the common block tables, and the GLM-Next cache
contract all use the logical block from `cache_config.block_size`.
Sizing persistent buffers from the spec overflows them by the
ceil-rounding slack (`required=1044` vs `capacity=1040` on the first
forward).
2. **GLM-Next layout.** The v2 MLA spec re-wrap dropped the
`model_version` / `compress_ratio` markers the cache-group
classification needs; the compressed indexer small page (compress_ratio
> 1) is a single-tensor overlay on a shared padded slot, not an MLA
latent/rope K/V pair; NoPE MLA layers legitimately carry an empty rope/V
component.
3. **Unequal TP.** Page-size unification is TP-dependent for hybrid
models (the Mamba state page scales with heads/TP), so a TP8 producer
and a TP4 consumer publish different unified block sizes for
byte-identical replicated caches — kernel blocks can no longer be paired
index-wise.

Changes:

- v2 attn_utils: propagate `model_version` /
`indexes_kv_by_block_stride` / `compress_ratio` /
`non_causal_multi_token_decode` through the MLA spec re-wrap; reshape
the compressed indexer small-page layer (compress_ratio > 1) as a single
strided tensor overlaid from byte zero of the shared padded slot.
- KPool indexer/tail backends: accept upstream's `cache_dtype_str` probe
kwarg; take the logical block size from `cache_config.block_size`.
- SFA metadata state: size the persistent block table buffer from the
cache config's logical block expansion instead of the spec's.
- Mooncake V2 connector: skip zero-size cache components when collecting
register ranges (their degenerate storage corrupts the range arithmetic)
and skip zero-length transfer entries the engine rejects with E19999.
- Unequal-TP: transfer replicated MLA/indexer caches as GCD-sized
token-segment byte runs (`_compute_cross_tp_runs`); transfer the indexer
tail whole-block instead of through the HND head-sharded path; raise
with the layer name on kernel-block-size mismatch.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes — it enables a new deployment topology: GLM-Next hybrid models can
now run PD disaggregation on MRV2 with `MooncakeConnectorV2` (pull
mode), including a TP8 producer feeding a DP2xTP4 consumer. Requires
`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1` and a kv-transfer-config with
`MooncakeConnectorV2`. No behavior change for existing models and
configurations: the new code paths are gated (the strided reshape only
triggers for MLA-family specs with compress_ratio > 1; the cross-TP run
path only activates when local and remote kernel block sizes differ; the
equal-TP block pairing path is unchanged).

### How was this patch tested?

- **Unit tests:** the `mooncake_v2` suite passes 150/150, covering
cross-TP run splitting/coalescing/computed-offset/bounds, tail
replica/whole-block mapping, bucket routing, and per-component address
scaling. The full UT sweep over
`tests/ut/{models,attention,worker,core,kv_offload}` produces a failure
set identical to upstream main (pre-existing failures only, none
introduced by this PR).
- **E2E, 10-layer GLM-5.3-Flash debug model:** 1P1D TP4/TP4 (producer
cards 0-3, consumer cards 4-7, eager), pull-mode KV transfer over the
mooncake engine relayed through a load-balance proxy: first-token
fidelity 18/18, outputs match the single-instance baseline to the
model's own determinism, real per-rank transfer logs, zero recompute
fallback.
- **E2E, full w8a8 GLM-5.3-Flash:** P=TP8 producer, D=DP2xTP4 consumer
(FULL_DECODE_ONLY graph mode): zero pull errors, ~18.5 MB transferred
per request, TextVQA accuracy consistent with the colocated baseline.

[BugFix][Attention] Split oversized A5 Sparse MLA cache pages (#16913)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Hybrid KDA/MLA cache alignment can produce attention storage pages
larger than the sparse attention operator limit. For GLM5Next with
DP8/TP1, the storage page is 4352 tokens, while SparseFlashMla accepts
an ori_kv block size of at most 1024.

The A2/A3 path already presents oversized storage pages as smaller
operator pages, but the A5 SparseFlashMla path kept the original
storage-page shape. This caused CANN tiling to reject ori_kv.shape[1] ==
4352.

This change:

- applies the sparse attention operator page limit to A5 metadata as
well;
- exposes oversized contiguous storage pages through a zero-copy
operator-page view;
- keeps the cache tensor, block table, and metadata in the same
128-token page units;
- rejects non-divisible or non-viewable layouts instead of copying or
silently misaddressing data;
- adds a regression case for the exact 4352-token storage page and
verifies token-address preservation.

The allocator-facing 4352-token storage page remains unchanged, so
KDA/MLA hybrid cache alignment is preserved.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No public API or configuration changes. A5 GLM5Next deployments with
oversized hybrid cache pages no longer pass an unsupported block size to
SparseFlashMla.

[CI] Switch nightly image build from Quay to SWR north-12 (#16299)

### Summary

Migrate the nightly image build & publish pipeline from Quay to SWR
(Huawei Cloud) **north-12**. The build now runs on cluster-internal
self-hosted runners with no public egress, so the whole build (git
clone, pip install, registry push) has been moved onto internal
mirrors/proxy.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

**Registry switch (Quay / southwest-2 → north-12)**

- daily →
`swr.cn-north-12.myhuaweicloud.com/atlas_inference/vllm-ascend` (temp:
`.../atlas_inference/vllm-atlas-temp`)
- release → `swr.cn-north-12.myhuaweicloud.com/ascend/vllm-ascend`
(temp: `.../atlas_ci/vllm-atlas-temp`)

**Build mechanism**

- Replace `docker build` + `docker push` with `docker buildx build
--push` against a remote buildkitd (running inside the CANN container).
- Add `--provenance=false --sbom=false` and `oci-mediatypes=false` so
buildx produces Docker v2 manifests that SWR accepts (SWR rejects OCI
attestation manifests / image index).
- Multi-arch merge via `docker buildx imagetools create`; each OS
variant merges independently and fails loudly when both arch images are
absent.

**Parameterized Dockerfiles (no hardcoded internal addresses)**

- Move `PIP_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_TRUSTED_HOST`,
`GIT_PROXY`, and benchmark `AIS_BENCH_*` to top-level `ARG`s.
- Defaults are the public community mirrors, so standalone `docker
build` is unaffected.
- CI overrides them via `--build-arg` with the in-cluster mirrors
(`cache-service.nginx-pypi-cache.svc.cluster.local`) and
`gh-proxy.test.osinfra.cn`.

[Feature][xlite] Support speculative decoding methods with a sequential causal chain (MTP, etc.) in xlite backend (#16669)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Enables MTP (and other speculative decoding methods with a **sequential
causal chain**) on the xlite backend. Previously the xlite docking only
handled standard decode; enabling a speculative config under
`xlite_graph_config` was rejected at startup, and the graph routing
inside the wrapper assumed non-speculative batch shapes.

The change is split across the docking layer:

- **`vllm_ascend/xlite/xlite.py`**: The `XliteWrapper` now routes
prefill/decode batches by **token budget** (comparing the forward
context's `max_tokens_across_dp` against a preallocated `max_m` limit)
instead of dispatching on the batch attention state. This makes the
wrapper agnostic to the different batch shapes that MTP produces
(decode, spec-decoding, and the draft model's sequential causal steps
all carry token counts above the decode threshold and are handled
uniformly by the xlite forward path). Metadata slicing, hidden-state
buffers and the inputs-embeds path are sized from the token budget
rather than the request count.
- **`vllm_ascend/xlite/xlite_model_runner.py`**: Adds a `_dummy_run`
override plus the `_bypass_xlite_wrapper` context manager so that
profile runs and graph-capture warmups execute on the native runnable
instead of the xlite forward (xlite can only serve real
decode/spec-decoding steps; a dummy batch would stall the runtime). DP
`execute_dummy_batch` still routes through xlite deliberately, to keep
ranks in sync. `initialize_kv_cache` additionally verifies that the
native attention builder's metadata class matches what the xlite adapter
expects, failing fast with an error instead of producing garbage at
runtime.
- **`vllm_ascend/xlite/xlite_worker.py`**: `compile_or_warm_up_model`
wraps the base warmup + capture sequence in the same bypass, covering
warmup dummy runs that do not carry the capture/profile flags
themselves.
- **`vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py`**:
`XliteGraphConfig._validate_preconditions` now explicitly whitelists the
supported speculative methods (`mtp`, `draft_model`,
`extract_hidden_states`), rejects aux-hidden-state methods (`eagle3`,
`dflash`, `dspark`) and pipeline parallelism, and warns on non-128 block
sizes. `init_ascend_config` is annotated to return `AscendConfig`.
- **`vllm_ascend/platform.py`**: The cudagraph-mode resolution for xlite
now accounts for speculative decoding: with MTP enabled the decode-side
graph mode falls back to `NONE` (eager decode) unless the composition
supports it, `spec_config.enforce_eager` is derived from the resolved
mode, and `full_mode` keeps the eager fallback behavior. Also moved
ahead of the `enforce_eager` handling so the resolved mode feeds into
it.
- **Docs** (`graph_mode`, `additional_config`): document the
token-budget routing semantics ("since v0.28.0") and the redefined
`full_mode` meaning.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, for users running the xlite backend on Atlas A3:

- **New capability**: MTP speculative decoding (methods with a
sequential causal chain) can now be combined with `xlite_graph_config`
(`xlite full` and `xlite decode-only`). Aux-hidden-state methods
(`eagle3`, `dflash`, `dspark`) and pipeline parallelism fail fast at
startup with a clear error.
- **Behavior change**: batch routing inside the xlite wrapper is now
based on the token budget (`max_m`) rather than the attention state —
batches whose token count exceeds the budget fall back to the native
runnable. Users relying on the previous dispatch semantics should note
the routing rule change (documented in `graph_mode.md`).

No public API or CLI flag is added/removed; configuration stays on the
existing `additional_config` / `graph-tokens` options.

### How was this patch tested?

We benchmarked model accuracies with `GLM-4.7-W8A8-floatmtp` and
`DeepSeek-V3.1-w8a8-mtp-QuaRot` using `aisbench`. The

[BugFix][Core] Fix MTP MoE finalize layout with upstream SP (#16081)

Remove the legacy draft VL TP all-reduce bypass from the EP
sequence-parallel finalize path and add regression coverage.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR fixes a token-layout mismatch when Qwen3.5 MTP is used together
with expert parallelism and upstream MoE sequence parallelism.

With upstream MoE sequence parallelism enabled,
`PrepareAndFinalizeWithAllGather` uses the following communication flow:

```text
TP AllGather
    -> Attention
    -> TP ReduceScatter
    -> EP AllGather
    -> MoE
    -> EP ReduceScatter
```

Therefore, `maybe_pad_and_reduce` is an EP sequence-parallel finalize
operation and must return the local EP/SP sequence shard.

However, it still contained a legacy draft-VL special case:

```python
if _EXTRA_CTX.is_draft_model and is_vl_model():
    return tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(x)
```

TP AllReduce preserves the global-token layout instead of restoring the
local EP/SP shard.

For Qwen3.5 MTP, this causes the draft model to return a tensor with an
unexpected token dimension, resulting in a deterministic shape mismatch
during profiling or execution, for example:

```text
4096 vs 1024
```

The real and fake implementations of this custom operation were also
inconsistent in this case:

- The real implementation returned the global-token shape through TP
AllReduce.
- The fake implementation always returned the local EP shard shape.

This special case originated from the FlashComm1 implementation. PR
#7683 explicitly restricted the draft-VL TP AllReduce bypass to non-EP
communication using `not is_ep_comm`.

After FlashComm1 was removed in #13946, `maybe_pad_and_reduce` became an
EP-only operation, but the legacy bypass remained without that guard.

This PR:

- Removes the obsolete draft-VL TP AllReduce bypass.
- Removes the corresponding unused imports.
- Makes the real implementation follow the same EP ReduceScatter
contract as the fake implementation.
- Adds a regression UT ensuring that draft-VL execution cannot bypass EP
ReduceScatter.
- Updates the existing four-card Qwen3.5 MTP test to explicitly cover:
  - DP=2
  - TP=2
  - Expert parallelism
  - Upstream MoE sequence parallelism
  - MTP with 3 speculative tokens

The fix is intentionally limited to the EP/SP finalize communication
layer. It does not add model-specific logic or introduce another
sequence-parallel configuration flag.

Related PRs: #7683, #13946

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes.

Qwen3.5 MoE models can now use MTP speculative decoding together with
DP, TP, EP, and upstream MoE sequence parallelism without failing
because of a token-dimension mismatch.

There are no API or configuration interface changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Regression coverage added:

- Added `test_sp_ep_reduce_scatter_draft_vl_keeps_ep_layout`.
- The test reproduces the historical draft-VL state and fails if the
EP/SP finalize path attempts to use TP AllReduce.
- The expected output remains the current EP rank's local token shard.
- Updated the existing Qwen3.5 four-card E2E case to explicitly use:
  - `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B`
  - DP=2
  - TP=2

[BugFix][MRV2] Align PCP slot dtype and preserve gathered DCP slots (#16775)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Fix two slot-mapping issues in PCP C8 cache writes:

1. Ascend PCP inherits upstream int64 global/gathered buffers and uses
them as the output of `compute_slot_mappings`, bypassing the normal
Ascend dtype adaptation. Initialize both persistent buffers and the
padding scalar with `block_tables.slot_mappings.dtype`, avoiding
per-forward conversion.
2. The DCP getter truncates the mapping to the local input-token count.
In PCP+DCP prefill/mixed batches, KV rows have already been gathered
across PCP ranks, so this truncation drops corresponding cache
destinations. Update the existing DCP getter to preserve the full
mapping for PCP prefill/mixed batches; ordinary DCP, DSA+DCP and pure
decode retain their existing slicing behavior.

Triggering scenarios:

- **Indexer C8:** MRV2 PCP + Indexer C8 on a PD producer enables the
optimized cache-write path. Its `store_kv_block_metadata` kernel reads
slots as int32, misinterpreting PCP's int64 buffer. The non-PD scatter
path does not use this kernel.
- **SFA C8:** PCP+DCP prefill/mixed batches defer the C8 cache write
until after PCP gathers KV. The write then receives a mapping truncated
to the local token count, rather than one slot per gathered KV row. This
was observed with PD, but the code path is not inherently limited to PD.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Fixes C8 cache-write correctness in the affected scenarios above. No API
or configuration changes.

### How was this patch tested?

Added regression unit tests:

- `test_pcp_slot_buffers_match_block_tables` in
`tests/ut/worker/test_pcp_manager_v2.py` verifies that PCP slot buffers
match the block-table slot dtype.
- `test_sfa_dcp_slot_mapping_matches_parallel_layout` in
`tests/ut/attention/test_sfa_cp.py` covers slot-mapping behavior across
PCP/DCP layouts.

[Performance] Enable AscendC index score decode for MiniMax-M3 (#16426)

### What this PR does / why we need it?

This PR ports the missing `MsaIndexScore` KV-splitting optimization from
ops-transformer PR 11754 onto the current vLLM Ascend `main`
implementation and enables the optimized bundled AscendC operator for
MiniMax-M3 index-score decode.

The operator port is intentionally narrow. It retains current mainline
hardware-profile dispatch, Catlass integration, and vLLM-specific
adapters while adding:

- the `kvChunks` tiling-data path for short-M/long-KV workloads;
- A2/A5 scheduler, wide-score flush, and writeback fixes;
- q4 x 275-block FP16/FP8 regression cases and source-level coverage;
- updated operator documentation.

The A5 decode follow-up removes the communication bottleneck around the
faster kernel:

- score the complete replicated index-K block table instead of using TP
block splitting and collectives;
- apply `init_blocks` and `local_blocks` in the AscendC epilogue for
this full-table path;
- reuse the existing A5 TopK postprocess kernel for final indices and
selection counts.

A2/A3 keep the existing TP-sharded decode path. The TP-sharded path
keeps candidate forcing in its TopK stage because the operator
attributes do not carry a global block offset.

Matched Ascend 950 profiling used MiniMax-M3, TP4 x DP2, decode-only
requests, and the maximum TP-rank duration within each synchronous DP
step. The complete layer path is measured after `ScatterPaCache` through
the final TopK output.

| Input / output | Original A5 Triton | Optimized AscendC | Change |
Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 16K / 1K | 22.802 us/layer | 20.579 us/layer | -9.75% | 1.108x |
| 128K / 1K | 57.011 us/layer | 26.735 us/layer | -53.11% | 2.132x |

At 128K, this saves 30.276 us per layer, or about 1.726 ms across the 57
sparse-attention layers in one model step. These are IndexScore
layer-path device-time observations, not end-to-end latency claims.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. MiniMax-M3 uses the bundled AscendC `MsaIndexScore` implementation
for both prefill and decode, including the optimized A5 full-table
decode path.

### How was this patch tested?

- rebased onto current `main` at
`125924bb2cb5ca3f68368f251c01c705d3a67b10`
- stable patch-id verified for the operator-sync commit after rebase
- `python -m py_compile` for the modified model, NPU helper, and
unit-test files
- `git diff --check`
- release-environment MiniMax-M3 unit test: 64 passed
- Ascend 950 `MsaIndexScore` package build for the operator-sync commit
- A5 service profiling with two 16K/1K and two 128K/1K requests; all
requests returned HTTP 200 with exact prompt/completion token counts,
and all eight DP2 x TP4 rank traces were generated

The latest-main three-file test overlay passed the new IndexScore cases;
six unrelated cases failed because the test container retained release
versions of the hardware-capability enum, scatter API, and C++ source
layout. Full main-environment validation is delegated to CI.
